title: deployment-nightshift-runlog-apr-2027
content:
Nightshift runlog — 2027-04-15 22:00 UTC -> 2027-04-16 04:30 UTC
Owner: Lena Rodriguez (notes + handoff)
Summary: Brief, focused night-run to triage a recurring onprem network flapping pattern observed in Zephyr Labs cluster (customer-facing VPC). Two main symptoms: intermittent gRPC stream resets causing >100ms tail latency spikes, and occasional KV cache warmup stalls after node cutover. No data leak or security alerts.

Goals for the shift:
- Stabilize the VPC peering path and confirm mitigation (temporary route preference)
- Capture traces for 3-4 repro windows and attach to JIRA-9123
- Validate KV cache warmup behavior after node replacement and put a mitigation patch in staging

Timeline / Events (UTC):
22:05 — shift start. Quick check: dashboards good, no active alerts.
22:18 — Ops alert: spike in 99th latency for zephyr-prod-vpc (trace id root: 010203fa). Noted gRPC reset pattern in logs from gw-node-7.
22:22 — Remote into gw-node-7; kernel dmesg shows repeated netlink messages about route flaps on eth1 (peer 10.8.3.0/24). Started packet capture (tcpdump -w /tmp/zephyr-flap-1.pcap).
22:35 — Opened JIRA-9123 (linked above) to track root cause; assigned to Marcus for routing config audit. Added initial hypothesis: intermittent BGP session resets on customer side causing transient path churn.
23:00 — Workaround applied: pinned primary egress via halo-pop-2 (policy override, 5m TTL). Observed immediate reduction in gRPC resets.
23:15 — Nightshift call with oncall SRE (Rohan) and SE (Aisha). Decided next steps: collect longer pcap, enable verbose grpc logging for 48h, and schedule a maintenance window with Zephyr networking team for 04/17.
00:30 — New symptom: after a scheduled node replacement (rolling) in zephyr-cache-1 pool, two requests hit node that reported empty KV cache and experienced cold-start penalty ~450ms for first few requests. This is captured in JIRA-9130.
00:45 — Reproduced KV cache warmup locally on a staging replica using the same model variant and sequence-length distribution. Root cause candidate: cache population relies on prefix caching daemon which failed to restart fast enough under constrained disk I/O during node provisioning.
01:10 — Temp fix: add prewarmed cache snapshot restore step to the install script (role: se-install). Patch created in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/1298 (branch: prewarm-kv-restore-night). Deployed to staging zephyr-stg.
01:55 — Observed staging: warmup reduced first-request delta from ~450ms to ~70ms. Good signal. Marked action item: include snapshot checksum check and backoff to avoid race with mount.
02:10 — Monitoring note: increased token consumption in zephyr-prod model-router during mitigation window (expected due to replays). Added temporary quota alert adjustments to avoid accidental throttling.
02:45 — Confirmed with Zephyr SE that their edge firewall logs show short BGP resets coincident with our timestamps; they will escalate internally. Coordination ticket: JIRA-9123 comment thread updated.
03:20 — Nightshift tidy: collected traces (trace ids: 010203fa, 010204ab, 010204cd), pcaps (/tmp/zephyr-flap-1.pcap, /tmp/zephyr-flap-2.pcap), and kv warmup logs (/var/log/kv-prewarm.log.*). Attached artifacts to both JIRAs.
03:45 — Handoff prep: wrote this runlog, enumerated action items and owners below. Set follow-up sync for 04/16 11:00 PT with Zephyr SE + Marcus + Rohan + Aisha.

Open action items:
- Marcus Lee: deep audit of peering config + BGP timers on halo-pop-2 and halo-pop-3. (JIRA-9123)
- Rohan Gupta: harden prefix caching daemon startup path; add backoff + retries for mount readiness. (PR in review: ops#1298)
- Aisha Patel: own customer comms and schedule 04/17 maintenance window; request Zephyr firewall team logs for 04/15 22:00-23:30 UTC.
- Lena Rodriguez: attach full pcaps and traces to JIRA entries, include sample grep commands, and draft a short postmortem outline (if incident reoccurs).

Notes to self / rough brainstorm:
- Consider introducing an install-time KV snapshot verification step: after mount, compute checksum, compare with metadata store. Avoids race where snapshot is not yet available.
- Investigate adding a small always-on cache population job during node boot to reduce cold-start impact for small clusters. Could be a fast-path that replays top-20 prefixes from telemetry.
- If BGP resets persist, evaluate fallback policy to route across second-pop for TCP long-lived connections (could be tricky for KV sync but worthwhile).

Risks / open questions:
- Will prewarming snapshots for every node increase storage/IO pressure at scale? Need cost estimate from infra.
- Does Zephyr's edge appliance vendor have known BGP firmware bugs? Aisha to push for vendor model and firmware version.

Handoff checklist (what I left configured):
- Temporary route pinning active (halo-pop-2) until 04/17 maintenance.
- Verbose gRPC logging enabled for 48h on gw-node-6/7.
- Staging prewarm patch deployed to zephyr-stg.
- Alerts: quotas adjusted and 99th-latency temporary suppression window documented in alert comment.

If you pick this up: first step — check traces for trace id 010203fa and confirm whether resets line up with peer BGP flaps; grab pcap /tmp/zephyr-flap-1.pcap from gw-node-7.

Quick links and commands (for whoever runs follow-up):
- Download pcap: scp ops@gw-node-7:/tmp/zephyr-flap-1.pcap ~/ ; tcpdump -r zephyr-flap-1.pcap
- Trace lookup: redwood-trace view 010203fa --span 0..1000
- JIRA tickets: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-9123 , https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-9130
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/1298

Last notes: overall outcome for the night is positive — mitigation reduced customer-facing tail spikes and a staging patch materially improved KV warmup. Remaining work is coordination with Zephyr networking team and merging the prewarm protection into the installer.

Lena Rodriguez
nightshift lead — eng-private-deployments
